criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Cover memo identifies LTC ratio exceeds 80% maximum
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover memorandum expressly identifies the LTC exceedance. Issue 1 in the top-risk register is titled 'Loan-to-cost of 83.77% against the Term Sheet's own 80% maximum; $2,140,000 over,' and Section 5.1 independently recomputes '$47,500,000 ÷ $56,700,000 = 83.7743%... exceeds 80.00% by 3.77 points ($2,140,000).' Issue 1's detailed analysis repeats the arithmetic and flags it as a breach of the Bank's own executed term sheet covenant. The criterion is satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Cover memo notes mezzanine loan doesn't count as borrower equity
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo repeatedly treats the $9,200,000 mezzanine loan as debt, not borrower equity. Section 3.1 states the sources and uses 'funds 100% of a $56,700,000 budget ... with $56,700,000 of debt' ($47,500,000 senior plus $9,200,000 mezzanine), and Issue 3 ('No genuine equity: the land cost is funded by the mezzanine loan') explains there is 'no equity in the structure that is not either (a) debt-funded or (b) to be replaced by the equity deposit.' It further notes the CM's 18.2% equity figure double-counts the land because the land cost was debt-funded, and connects this to the LTC/equity deficiency requiring the $2,140,000 Equity Deposit. While the memo doesn't use the exact entity name 'Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC' or phrase 'under the bank's underwriting policy,' the substantive distinction required by the criterion—that the mezzanine is debt and cannot serve as borrower equity, contributing to the LTC/equity shortfall—is clearly made.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Cover memo quantifies equity shortfall (~$2,140,000)
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover memorandum expressly quantifies the equity shortfall at approximately $2,140,000. In the top-risk register (Issue 1) it states 'Loan-to-cost of 83.77% against the Term Sheet's own 80% maximum; $2,140,000 over' and recommends a verified '$2,140,000 equity deposit.' Section 5 independently computes the maximum loan at 80% LTC as $56,700,000 × 80% = $45,360,000, and states the loan 'exceeds 80.00% by 3.77 points ($2,140,000).' The $2,140,000 figure equals $47,500,000 − $45,360,000, matching the criterion's expected calculation. The figure is also used consistently in the equity-escrow discussion (Issues 3 and 4) and the drafting recommendations (Draft §4.8).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Loan agreement includes equity escrow or restructuring mechanism
criteria_results.reasoning: The draft loan agreement contains multiple operative provisions implementing an equity escrow mechanism to address the LTC gap. Section 1.1 defines 'Equity Deposit' ($2,140,000, or such greater amount as needed so LTC does not exceed 80.00%) and 'Equity Escrow Account.' Section 3.3 makes delivery of the Equity Deposit into the Equity Escrow Account a condition precedent to closing, with source-of-funds certification. Section 4.8 (Equity First; Equity Deposit) requires the deposit, restricts its application to Eligible Costs before Advances, prohibits replenishment from borrowed funds, and requires increases/reductions to maintain 80.00% LTC. Section 2.1(b) imposes an LTC Availability borrowing-base cap of $45,360,000 based on Total Project Costs, and Section 4.2(h) makes compliance with Section 4.8 (Equity First) a condition to each Advance. Sections 8.1 and 8.2 test LTC/LTV, and Exhibit A/B (Advance Request and Compliance Certificate) confirm the Equity Deposit application and LTC compliance. Schedule 1.1 notes reconcile the Equity Deposit to the 80.00% LTC. The agreement plainly includes a structural mechanism (equity escrow) curing the LTC exceedance as a closing condition and condition to advances.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Cover memo identifies interest reserve may be insufficient
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover memorandum expressly identifies the interest reserve adequacy issue as a High-risk item (Issue 22), stating that the $4,850,000 reserve is short by approximately $361,500 at a 4.35% SOFR assumption and by approximately $1,047,000 at +100 bps, with a detailed monthly-model analysis, a risk register entry, and recommendations (resize the reserve or add a replenishment covenant, Draft §§2.10, 4.2(g), 10.16). This directly satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Cover memo notes below-market SOFR assumption in budget
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies the below-market SOFR assumption. Issue 22 states that the Draw Schedule's interest reserve analysis assumes 3.50% SOFR 'when the current rate is approximately 4.35%) is 85 basis points below current market,' and concludes the Draw Schedule's 'APPEARS ADEQUATE' conclusion is correct only at 3.50% SOFR. Section 5's verification table likewise flags the discrepancy and quantifies the shortfall at the CM's 4.35% assumption and at stressed rates. The criterion is satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Loan agreement requires borrower to fund interest reserve shortfalls
criteria_results.reasoning: The loan agreement expressly addresses interest reserve insufficiency. Section 2.10(c) establishes periodic adequacy testing (at each Advance Request and at least quarterly). Section 2.10(d) requires Borrower to fund any Interest Reserve Deficiency (defined in 2.10(c)) from its own funds within five Business Days after notice, and expressly bars funding from Loan proceeds, Mezzanine Loan proceeds, the Equity Deposit or other borrowed funds. Section 2.10(e) addresses exhaustion, Section 2.7 requires Borrower to pay interest from its own funds after exhaustion, and Section 10.16 makes failure to fund an Interest Reserve Deficiency an Event of Default. Related mechanics appear in Section 4.2(g), the Exhibit A Advance Request certification, and Schedule 6.8 monthly reconciliation reporting.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Cover memo identifies conflicting pledges of membership interests
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover memorandum expressly identifies the conflict in Issue 6: the senior construction loan requires a pledge of 100% of membership interests, while the mezzanine loan is also secured by a pledge of 100% of membership interests in the Borrower. It explains that only one lender can hold a first-priority security interest in the same collateral and recommends an intercreditor agreement giving the Bank first priority. The issue is also included in the top-risk register.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Cover memo recommends intercreditor agreement as closing condition
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover memorandum addresses the double-pledge of membership interests in Issue 6 and explicitly recommends (a) an intercreditor agreement giving the Bank (senior lender) first priority over the mezzanine lender, and (b) making execution of the intercreditor agreement a 'non-waivable condition to the first advance.' This is reinforced in Section 7.1 (Issue 6 mapping to Draft §13.2 intercreditor terms, noted as 'intercreditor not yet available'), in Section 10.1(c) (requesting the intercreditor draft), and in Section 8's diligence list. The criterion is therefore satisfied: the memo proposes a resolution—first-priority senior pledge plus intercreditor agreement as a closing/advance condition.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Loan agreement conditions closing on executed intercreditor agreement
criteria_results.reasoning: The draft expressly makes execution and delivery of the Intercreditor Agreement a closing condition. Recital D conditions the Loan on an intercreditor agreement among Lender, Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC (the Mezzanine Lender) and Borrower; Section 3.1 lists the Intercreditor Agreement among the Loan Documents to be delivered at closing; and Section 3.9 specifically provides that 'Execution and delivery of the Intercreditor Agreement ... shall be a non-waivable condition to the Initial Advance and to each subsequent Advance.' Article XIII further resolves the competing pledge by subordinating Mezzanine Lender's pledge of the membership interests to Lender's first-priority pledge and imposing standstill, cure and purchase-option terms. The criterion is satisfied (the only defects are minor internal cross-reference/numbering inconsistencies, e.g., TOC versus body ordering of Sections 3.9–3.14, which do not affect the substantive closing condition).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Cover memo identifies NFA residential use restriction conflict
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo expressly identifies the NFA use restriction conflict: it notes the NCDEQ NFA restricts the 0.38-acre northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102 to non-residential use (Section 4.1 Environmental framework, Issue 18) and that the project plans place residential units above that area, referencing the CM's assertion of 14 units above the restricted area (Issue 18 in Section 6, and the risk register row 18–19 in Section 3.2). It discusses the inconsistency, questions the 14-unit figure as unsourced, and recommends resolution. The criterion is satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Cover memo discusses impact on appraised value and leasing
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover memorandum extensively discusses the valuation and leasing impact of the NFA residential use restriction. In the top-risk register (Issue 18–19) it states the restriction 'Affects certificates of occupancy for part of the unit mix, DSCR and appraised value.' Issue 18 analyzes that the CM's assertion of 14 affected units is unsourced, quantifies the revenue impact ($377,160), recalculates DSCR to 1.21x (below the 1.25x covenant), notes possible overstatement of as-completed and as-stabilized value, and recommends asking the appraiser to confirm whether any value was attributed to the affected units. Section 5.1 and Issue 16 similarly tie valuation consequences to NOI adjustments. This fully satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Loan agreement includes environmental compliance covenant or CP
criteria_results.reasoning: The loan agreement extensively addresses the NFA use restriction. Section 3.6 (Conditions Precedent) requires evidence of NFA compliance, including NCDEQ approval of the soil management plan, recording of the deed notice, and—critically—Section 3.6(d) requires either an NCDEQ modification to the NFA Letter permitting residential occupancy, a redesign eliminating residential occupancy above the Affected Area, or another Lender-approved resolution. Section 5.8 (Representation) affirmatively represents that the NFA Letter is in full force and effect, all conditions satisfied, and that no residential occupancy is or will be permitted in the Affected Area except as approved by NCDEQ. Section 6.4 (Covenant) expressly prohibits residential occupancy in the Affected Area unless NCDEQ issues a written modification permitting such use and Lender consents, and requires compliance with all NFA conditions including the vapor mitigation system and soil management plan. Sections 7.7 and 10.11 reinforce this (prohibited use and Event of Default), and Schedule 1.4 details each NFA condition. This fully satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Cover memo identifies borrower has zero direct cash equity
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover memorandum explicitly identifies zero direct cash equity in multiple places. Section 3.1 states the capital structure 'contains no genuine cash equity: the sources and uses presented to the Bank funds 100% of a $56,700,000 budget ... with $56,700,000 of debt.' Section 5.1 notes the only equity line is $0 ($47,500,000 + $9,200,000 + $0 = $56,700,000). Section 5.1's post-closing book equity row states equity of '$0, or $2,140,000 after the equity deposit.' Issue 3 is devoted to the absence of genuine equity, and the risk register captures it. The criterion is satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Cover memo discusses circular affiliate funding concern
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo substantively addresses the Brightleaf affiliate funding concern in several places: Issue 9 states the affiliation 'runs in three directions at once (member, mezzanine lender and fee recipient)'; Issue 6 identifies Brightleaf Investors Group LLC (controlled by Mr. Chen) as the affiliate of the mezzanine lender holding the competing pledge and whose consent/subordination is required; Issue 8 addresses the affiliate's veto over refinancing. On the funding side, the memo quotes the CM's statement that the land was funded 'through capital calls from all three members, including Brightleaf Investors Group LLC,' notes that Brightleaf received 28% for a $0 contribution 'in consideration of its commitment to arrange third-party mezzanine financing,' and explains in Issues 3 and 4 that the $9.2M mezzanine loan from that affiliate is used to reimburse the $8.2M land cost and fund the developer fee — i.e., a return of member capital funded by an affiliate's loan, which the draft then prohibits (Draft §§2.2, 4.16, 7.4). Although the memo does not name 'Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC' or use the word 'circular' for this specific pair, the affiliation and the round-trip funding flows are identified and analyzed with recommended resolutions, satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Loan agreement requires evidence of equity contribution as CP
criteria_results.reasoning: The draft includes a condition precedent in Section 3.3 requiring delivery of the Equity Deposit to the Equity Escrow Account, evidence of the source of funds, and a certification that the deposit is independently derived and not borrowed. Section 4.8 further addresses the Equity Deposit and LTC adequacy. This constitutes a condition precedent requiring verification of the borrower's equity contribution, satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Cover memo identifies unsatisfied prior deed of trust
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover memorandum expressly identifies the pre-existing, recorded but unsatisfied deed of trust held by Triangle Commercial Bank (recorded in Book 6215, Page 892, dated September 14, 2018, original principal $3,400,000, with no cancellation recorded) as shown in the Title Commitment (Sch. B-II Ex. 10 / Sch. B-I Req. 4). It is listed as a High-risk item in the top-risk register (Issue 13) with a recommended resolution requiring a payoff letter, funding of the payoff from Borrower equity rather than loan proceeds, a recorded cancellation/satisfaction, and deletion of the title exception at or before closing; it is also addressed in detail in Section 6.D (Issue 13) and mapped to draft provisions (§§3.5(b), 9.1, Schedule 1.3). The criterion is fully satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Loan agreement requires payoff/release of prior DOT as CP
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 3.5(b) of the conditions precedent expressly requires, as a condition to the Initial Advance/Closing, 'evidence of the release, satisfaction or recording of a payoff and cancellation of the deed of trust recorded in Book 6215, Page 892, Durham County Registry, in favor of Triangle Commercial Bank (original principal amount $3,400,000), pursuant to a payoff letter...' This is reinforced by Section 9.1 (the Triangle deed of trust 'must be released of record at or before Closing'), by the requirement in 3.5(a) that the Title Policy insure the Deed of Trust as a first-priority lien subject only to Permitted Exceptions, and by Schedule 1.3, which expressly excludes the Triangle DOT from the Permitted Exceptions and requires its release/satisfaction or removal of record at or before Closing. The criterion is satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Cover memo identifies SPE/affiliate substantive consolidation risk
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover memorandum identifies the SPE/affiliate conflict and its consolidation implications in multiple places. Issue 8 expressly states that Brightleaf Investors Group LLC (28% member) is an affiliate of the mezzanine lender and that 'The affiliate of the mezzanine lender can therefore block any refinancing...' Issue 6 further notes the interests are controlled 'through Mr. Chen, who controls both entities.' Issue 9 is captioned around the absence of SPE covenants and observes that 'the affiliation runs in three directions at once (member, mezzanine lender and fee recipient)' and that the entity protections the Bank assumes 'do not exist today,' while requiring a non-consolidation opinion as a closing condition (Draft §3.10). The memo thus links the borrower's member structure (Brightleaf Investors Group LLC being an affiliate of the mezzanine lender) to the absence of SPE/separateness covenants and the need for a non-consolidation opinion, which is the substantive consolidation protection. Therefore the SPE/affiliate substantive-consolidation risk is identified.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Cover memo recommends SPE protections (independent directors, non-consolidation opinions, anti-commingling)
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover memorandum expressly recommends multiple specific SPE protections. Issue 9 recommends making the operating agreement amendment (separateness/SPE covenants), the appointment of an independent manager, member resolutions, and a non-consolidation opinion closing conditions (Draft §§3.2, 3.10, 6.9), and notes the current absence of independent-manager and separateness provisions. Issue 8 further recommends independent-manager approval for insolvency filings (Draft §6.9(l)). Section 7.1 maps Issues 8–9 to §6.9 single-purpose entity covenants (a)–(n), operating agreement amendments, and the non-consolidation opinion, and Section 8 lists the non-consolidation opinion as a required pre-closing deliverable. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Loan agreement includes SPE covenants addressing affiliate separation
criteria_results.reasoning: The draft contains extensive SPE covenants in Section 6.9 (Single-Purpose Entity Covenants) that expressly address affiliate separateness: subsection (d) requires maintaining separate books, records, financial statements, bank accounts and tax returns from Members/Affiliates; subsection (e) prohibits commingling funds with any Member, Affiliate or other Person; subsection (i) requires all transactions with Members and Affiliates to be on arm's-length terms and documented; and subsection (l) requires at least one independent manager meeting independence criteria and holding a required vote on bankruptcy/insolvency filings. These are reinforced by the Section 5.13 SPE representation, Section 7.6 affiliate-transaction covenant, and Section 10.10 Event of Default for SPE covenant breaches. The criterion is satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Cover memo or loan agreement includes SOFR fallback/benchmark replacement
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 2.6 ("Benchmark Replacement") expressly addresses discontinuation/unrepresentativeness of Daily Simple SOFR, triggering a replacement-rate mechanism that references the ARRC recommended fallback language for commercial real estate loans, including the hardwired waterfall, corresponding spread adjustments, and mechanical/conforming changes. Supporting definitions and interest mechanics (Daily Simple SOFR, Business Day tied to SOFR publication, SOFR Floor, usury cap) are also present, and the term appears in the table of contents. Although the amendment process is framed as good-faith negotiation with an interim lender-selected rate rather than a fully self-executing hardwired waterfall, the document does contain benchmark replacement/SOFR fallback provisions consistent with ARRC recommendations, satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Cover memo identifies need for SOFR benchmark replacement provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: The criterion requires the cover memorandum to identify the need for SOFR benchmark replacement/fallback provisions (e.g., ARRC-recommended fallback language, benchmark replacement waterfall, conforming changes) given the loan's use of Daily Simple SOFR over a multi-year term. The memo mentions SOFR throughout, but only in the context of pricing (Daily Simple SOFR + 3.25%/3.50%, 1.00% SOFR floor) and interest-reserve rate assumptions (3.50%, 4.35%, stressed rates of 7.60%/8.60% all-in). Nowhere does it discuss benchmark transition risk, ARRC fallback language, a benchmark replacement waterfall, or conforming changes to the loan documents. No issue in the register, no diligence item, and no observation in Section 9 addresses SOFR fallback/transition. Accordingly the memo does not satisfy the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Cover memo discusses completion guaranty
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover memorandum explicitly discusses the completion guaranty as part of the guaranty structure. Section 4.1 lists 'Guaranties: Completion, carry and 25% partial repayment ($11,875,000)...' Issue 25 references the Completion Guaranty funding obligation, Issue 24 references aligning the Completion Guaranty date, and Section 9.3 addresses the carry guaranty versus interest reserve overlap. The completion guaranty is clearly discussed.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Cover memo discusses 25% partial repayment guaranty at $11,875,000 each
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover memorandum expressly discusses the 25% partial repayment guaranty at $11,875,000 and flags the conflict that the Credit Memorandum describes it as '$11,875,000 per guarantor' while the Term Sheet treats it as an aggregate joint-and-several cap (Issue 10). It therefore satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Cover memo addresses need for bad boy carve-out triggers
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover memorandum addresses the 'bad boy' carve-out in Section 4.1 (Transaction snapshot), which lists the guaranty structure as including 'Completion, carry and 25% partial repayment ($11,875,000), joint and several, with "bad boy" full-recourse springing events; unlimited environmental indemnity (Term Sheet §§7.1–7.4).' This expressly acknowledges the full-recourse springing triggers that convert the partial repayment guaranty. The memo also substantively discusses the related bad-boy trigger categories: voluntary bankruptcy/insolvency filings (Issue 8 and §6.9(l) requiring independent-manager approval), unauthorized transfers/governance vetoes (Issues 8–9 and operating agreement amendments), and environmental liability (the unlimited environmental indemnity and the extensive Section E environmental analysis). Guaranty carve-outs are therefore discussed rather than omitted.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Loan agreement or guaranty provisions include bad boy carve-outs
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 9.7(d) of the draft loan agreement, titled 'Bad Boy Carve-Outs,' expressly provides that the Partial Repayment Guaranty becomes a full recourse guaranty of 100% of the Obligations upon specified events, including fraud or intentional misrepresentation, voluntary bankruptcy/insolvency filing, unauthorized transfer or encumbrance of collateral, breach of SPE covenants, environmental liability or release of Hazardous Materials, waste of collateral, and misapplication of Insurance Proceeds, Condemnation Awards, rents or trust funds. This matches the criterion's requirement for bad boy carve-out triggers converting the partial repayment guaranty to full recourse.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Addresses NC foreclosure considerations for guaranty
criteria_results.reasoning: The output addresses North Carolina-specific foreclosure considerations relevant to the guaranty. The cover memorandum Section 9.1 discusses N.C.G.S. § 45-21.36, the fair-value determination for deficiencies, and confirmatory review with North Carolina counsel before finalizing guaranty forms. The loan agreement also expressly references N.C.G.S. § 45-21.36 in Sections 9.9 and 11.2 and preserves non-waivable guarantor protections in Section 11.10, thereby addressing guaranty enforceability and survival in the foreclosure context.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Cover memo identifies unspecified extension option conditions
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover memorandum discusses the 6-month extension option in several places, including its date, extension fee, and a DSCR extension test drawn from the Credit Memorandum. However, it does not identify that the term sheet's extension option states conditions are 'to be determined' or 'subject to customary conditions' without enumerating them, nor does it flag that the drafter must establish specific extension conditions. The memo therefore does not satisfy the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Loan agreement specifies at least 4 extension conditions
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 2.13(c) expressly enumerates multiple extension conditions, including no Event of Default, Substantial Completion plus final certificate of occupancy, a 75% leasing/occupancy threshold, a DSCR condition based on actual trailing NOI, payment of the Extension Fee, execution of an interest rate cap agreement, and continued effectiveness of the Intercreditor Agreement. This exceeds the requirement of at least four specified extension conditions.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Cover memo or loan agreement addresses retainage release and NC lien law
criteria_results.reasoning: The loan agreement's Section 4.4 expressly conditions the Final Advance/retainage release on final unconditional lien waivers under N.C.G.S. Chapter 44A, expiration of the Chapter 44A lien filing period without a lien claim, or bonding off/removal of any filed lien, and a title date-down. It also notes the corrected retainage amount ($3,475,000 versus the $3,275,000 source figure) and connects the release to North Carolina construction lien requirements, satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Loan agreement retainage release conditions include lien waivers
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 4.4 ('The Final Advance (Retainage Release)') expressly conditions the release of the 10% Retainage on: (a) Substantial Completion and issuance of a final certificate of occupancy for all residential and retail space; (b) the Architect's certificate of final completion; (c) delivery of final, unconditional lien waivers and releases in statutory form under N.C.G.S. Chapter 44A from the Contractor, all subcontractors and all materialmen; and (d) either expiration of the statutory lien-filing period under N.C.G.S. Chapter 44A without any claim of lien, or bonding off/removal of any lien filed. These satisfy all four (indeed, well more than the required two) of the enumerated criteria, including the express lien-waiver requirement. The condition is reinforced in Section 4.3(b), which bars disbursement of Retainage until Section 4.4's conditions are met.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Cover memo identifies CC&R architectural review as potential delay risk
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover memorandum identifies the Brightleaf Historic District Association CC&Rs and expressly flags architectural review as a potential construction delay risk. In Section 2 the title commitment is described as including 'the Brightleaf Historic District CC&Rs,' and Issue 16 (rated Medium) is dedicated to the architectural review issue: it notes that ARC approval is assumed by the Appraisal but unevidenced, that the title officer warns the Association may seek injunctive relief 'including to halt construction,' and that the CC&Rs' 90-day submission / 60-day approval (or deemed approval) timing 'may already be incompatible with a February 28, 2025 closing and a prompt construction start.' It also recommends making ARC approval or deemed approval a closing condition (Draft §3.5(f)). While the memo does not cite the specific recording reference (Book 6984, Page 1155), it does identify the Declaration of CC&Rs from the Brightleaf Historic District Association and squarely raises the architectural review/design standards delay risk, which is the substance of the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Loan agreement requires evidence of CC&R/design approval as CP
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 3.5(f) expressly makes it a condition precedent to closing that the Borrower deliver 'evidence that the ARC has approved the Approved Plans or that the applicable review period has lapsed (deemed approval), in each case as required by Article V of the CC&Rs.' The ARC is defined as the Architectural Review Committee of the Brightleaf Historic District Association. Additional related protections appear in Section 5.9 (representation that Approved Plans comply with the CC&Rs), Section 4.12(f) (Change Orders affecting any element subject to ARC review require Lender's prior written consent), Section 6.10(g) (notice of any suspension, revocation or challenge of ARC approval), and Section 10.15 (ARC approval revocation as a default event). The CC&R/design review requirement is therefore fully addressed.

criteria_results.title: Loan agreement correctly states loan amount as $47,500,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The agreement consistently states the maximum loan/commitment amount as $47,500,000: Recital B ('principal amount of $47,500,000'), the definition of 'Commitment' ('principal amount of $47,500,000'), 'Loan Amount' ('$47,500,000'), the Note (principal amount of the Commitment), Section 2.1, and Schedule 1.1 (Senior Loan commitment of $47,500,000). While a borrowing-base/LTC limitation caps actual advances at $45,360,000 absent increases in Total Project Costs, the commitment amount itself is correctly stated as $47,500,000, satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Loan agreement correctly identifies Lender as Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A.
criteria_results.reasoning: The loan agreement consistently identifies the Lender as Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A., including in the cover/preamble ("PINNACLE SAVINGS BANK, N.A., as Lender"), the notice address table for Lender, and the signature block ("PINNACLE SAVINGS BANK, N.A." with David Forsythe as SVP). The Lender is neither misnamed nor omitted.

criteria_results.title: Loan agreement correctly identifies Borrower as Harborview Capital Partners LLC
criteria_results.reasoning: The loan agreement consistently identifies the Borrower as Harborview Capital Partners LLC — in the cover/preamble ('HARBORVIEW CAPITAL PARTNERS LLC, as Borrower'), Recital A, the notice provisions, signature blocks, and the exhibits. The Borrower is not misnamed or omitted.

criteria_results.title: Loan agreement states construction period rate as Daily Simple SOFR + 3.25%
criteria_results.reasoning: The agreement defines the Applicable Rate during the Construction Period as the lesser of Daily Simple SOFR plus 3.25% per annum and the Maximum Lawful Rate, subject to the SOFR Floor. This matches the criterion's required construction period rate structure of Daily Simple SOFR + 3.25%.

criteria_results.title: Loan agreement states SOFR floor of 1.00%
criteria_results.reasoning: The agreement defines the 'SOFR Floor' as 1.00% per annum in Article I, and Section 2.5 expressly states that if Daily Simple SOFR is less than 1.00% on any day, it is deemed to be 1.00% for purposes of calculating the Applicable Rate, confirming a minimum Applicable Rate of 4.25% during the Construction Period (1.00% floor + 3.25% spread). The floor applies throughout, including the construction period.

criteria_results.title: Loan agreement states correct mini-perm interest rate
criteria_results.reasoning: The agreement defines the Applicable Rate during the Mini-Perm Period as Daily Simple SOFR plus 3.50% per annum, subject to the SOFR Floor, and defines the SOFR Floor as 1.00% per annum. Thus the rate, spread, and floor are correct.

criteria_results.title: Loan agreement states correct default rate
criteria_results.reasoning: The loan agreement defines the Default Rate as the lesser of (a) the Applicable Rate plus 5.00% per annum and (b) the Maximum Lawful Rate, satisfying the criterion that the default rate premium is 5.00%.

criteria_results.title: Loan agreement states correct construction maturity date
criteria_results.reasoning: The agreement defines the Construction Maturity Date as 30 months after the Closing Date, with an outside date of August 28, 2027, which matches the criterion assuming a February 28, 2025 closing.

criteria_results.title: Loan agreement states correct mini-perm maturity date
criteria_results.reasoning: The agreement defines the Mini-Perm Maturity Date as 12 months after the Construction Maturity Date and expressly states that, assuming a February 28, 2025 closing, it is August 28, 2028. This matches the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Loan agreement includes the 6-month extension option
criteria_results.reasoning: The agreement expressly includes an Extension Option in Section 2.13(c) permitting Borrower to extend the Mini-Perm Maturity Date by six months, and defines the Extended Maturity Date as February 28, 2029. This satisfies the criterion for a one-time 6-month extension of the mini-perm period to approximately February 28, 2029.

criteria_results.title: Loan agreement states correct origination fee
criteria_results.reasoning: The loan agreement states in Section 2.9(a) that the origination fee is $475,000, equal to 1.00% of the $47,500,000 Commitment, and is payable at Closing. This matches the criterion's required percentage and dollar amount.

criteria_results.title: Loan agreement includes exit fee of 0.50% during construction period
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 2.9(b) of the draft expressly provides for an Exit Fee equal to (i) 0.50% of the outstanding principal balance repaid if repayment occurs during the Construction Period, (ii) 0.25% during the first six months of the Mini-Perm Period, and (iii) zero thereafter. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Loan agreement includes exit fee of 0.25% during first 6 months of mini-perm

criteria_results.title: Loan agreement includes disbursement/draw schedule with milestones

criteria_results.title: Loan agreement includes 10% retainage holdback on hard costs

The schedule's note permitting a possible reduction to 5% after 50% completion does not alter the specified 10% baseline holdback.

criteria_results.title: Loan agreement includes correct collateral (first priority deed of trust)

criteria_results.title: Loan agreement includes minimum net worth covenant ($12,000,000 annually)

criteria_results.title: Loan agreement includes minimum guarantor liquidity covenant ($5,000,000 quarterly)

criteria_results.title: Loan agreement states correct partial repayment guaranty (25% / $11,875,000 each)
